chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Abdullah ibn Rashid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The man descends into the grave of his father, and the father does not descend into the grave of his son.
ai.seo_question: Can a father be buried in the same grave as his son according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This concise hadith from al-Kafi establishes a distinct asymmetry in Shia burial jurisprudence, permitting a son to share his father's grave while prohibiting the reverse. This ruling reflects the hierarchical status of the father as the primary ancestor and head of the family, a principle deeply rooted in the transmission chains of the Ahl al-Bayt. It serves as a foundational text for understanding the specific legal nuances of grave sharing (tadfin) in Shia fiqh.
